thread:
devon: Quick heads-up — ran smoke bring-up for veridian-v2 int4 (onboard candidate). Seeing a reproducible detok/tokenization issue in vertical Japanese texts with kanbun annotations and stacked hanzi; ruby/furigana almost entirely dropped in many outputs.
ci-bot: Smoke summary uploaded: s3://redwood-smoke/veridian-v2/int4/1795011111
ci-bot: Metrics: BLEU_delta: -3.2, token_mismatch_rate: +12.4% (kana-han boundaries), sample_count: 1200
alana: Is this happening on fp16 baseline too or only quantized variants?
devon: fp16 baseline looks fine. int8 small delta (~-0.4 BLEU), int4 much worse. I reproduced locally with the emu and on dedicated qsim.
ben: Runtime note: the int4 codepath recently switched to the fused-gemm quant kernel (PR #4453). Could be rounding/packing for multi-byte graphemes. Also rolled zwnj-normalizer last week.
mei: Linguistic context: kanbun marks control reading order for vertical classical Japanese; they often attach to hanzi clusters and route as ruby/furigana. If tokenizer collapses boundary tokens, the model loses attachment points -> translation drops.
devon: Example (original vertical snippet):
```
漢文︸（…）
乍起
　　　　☞ ︙
```
Model (int4) output: "乍起" -> missing furigana and merged with following kana: "乍起に\n"
Model (fp16) output: "乍起（さっき）に\n" — preserves reading.
alana: Can you paste the exact tokenization diff (fp16 vs int4) for that sample? We need to know which subtokens merged.
devon: pasted token diffs to thread: fp16: [0x3a,0x7f,0xA1,...] int4: [0x3a,0x7f,0xA1A2,...] — looks like a fused subtoken sequence in int4 where two bytes collapsed into one token id.
ben: That suggests our quantized embedding lookup or post-tokenizer packing might be emitting merged token ids when byte pairs are near boundary. Repro attempt: running qsim with --dump-token-ids --qconfig perchannel.
ci-bot: Job kicked: j-12345 (veridian-v2 int4 perchannel re-run). ETA ~12m.
me i: Minor suggestion — ensure pretokenizer normalizes vertical punctuation and keeps ZWJ/ZWNJ markers intact around ruby markers. Our locale preproc strip may be too aggressive.
alana: I'll add a focused eval: 2k vertical-kanbun/ruby samples, measure detok-match rate for furigana/ruby (% preserved), BLEU, and token-mismatch heatmap. PR for dataset coming in ~30m.
devon: ran quick ablation locally: switching qparams to --qbits=4 --sym-params=perchannel reduces the delta to -0.9 BLEU for the sample set (vs -3.2). So not all quant configs are equal.
ben: CI job j-12345 finished — ci-bot posted results: perchannel quant reduced token_mismatch to +3.1%, BLEU_delta now -0.8. Symmetric quant still worse.
ci-bot: Logs: s3://redwood-smoke/veridian-v2/int4/j-12345/logs
mei: This supports tokenizer+packing sensitivity. If perchannel works better, we may need to pin quant config for vertical-locale canaries or adjust the packing kernel to avoid merging adjacent grapheme bytes.
alana: Action items: (1) add vertical-kanbun dataset to regression suite (PR #5882), (2) add tokenizer normalization toggle to harness so we can flip ZWJ/ZWNJ preservation flags in evals, (3) hold veridian-v2-int4 canary rollout until we confirm no user-facing regressions for JP/vertical locales.
devon: I'll hold the canary promotion. Also opening an engineering triage: ENG-ML task to bisect the quant kernel (assign to @ben) and tokenization team to add normalization exceptions (assign to @mei).
ben: Starting kernel bisect now, will ping results here. If we can keep perchannel as safe default for now, we can proceed with limited rollout while we fix packing.
rachel: Thanks folks — PM note: keep me updated. Holding dedicated pool promotion until we see green on the new regression. @infra FYI.
alana: adding :eyes: and will update when PRs land.
devon: Thanks — will update thread with dataset PR and any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
